messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Ops OKR synthesis & decision lanes — week of Nov 30

Team —

Short synthesis ahead of QBR prep: pulled key signals from weekly OKR tracker (attached) and surfaced the top wins, current risks, and decision lanes where I need leadership guidance by EOW Nov 27. Please read the bullets and call out any disagreements inline.

Wins
- Serving runtime throughput: sustained 98% of target on p50 latency after kernel patch (prod canaries green).
- Redwood Dedicated: first customer (Acme Data) onboarding completed staging tests; integration sprint finished ahead of schedule.
- Observability: token-level cost dashboards are live for beta customers; initial anomalies flagged and triaged.

Top risks
1) Capacity procurement timeline for Dedicated GPU pool (affects Dec 6 SLA). Current quote from CloudVendor shows 3–4 week lead; procurement timeline mismatch could force a temporary burst fallback.
2) OKR ENG-3 (quantization rollout): we see output quality drift on a small subset of prompts after 8-bit rollout. Need to decide rollback vs. narrower rollout.
3) QBR narrative: we need a short one-pager that ties performance to projected unit economics (ask below).

Decision lanes / Asks (owners + due dates)
- Approve reallocation of $150k buffer to cover expedited procurement if CloudVendor cannot meet Dec 6 — owner: Markus — due: Nov 27 EOD.
- Direction on quantization: full rollback to previous model vs. graduated rollout (approve plan below) — owner: Vivek — due: Nov 26 COB.
- Approve QBR one-pager draft (attached) and confirm 2 slides for exec deck — owner: Laura — due: Nov 27 noon.
- Marissa: coordinate procurement communications with CloudVendor and Acme Data; attach timeline/quote and escalate if lead time slips — due: Nov 27 EOD.

Attachments: OKR_tracker_2026-11-23.xlsx (spreadsheet), QBR_one-pager_2026.pdf (one-pager)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR-summaries/ev-ops-weekly
HubSpot: HS-34752 (Acme Data onboarding)

Thanks — short bullets please so the follow-up thread stays actionable.

—
Evelyn Hart
VP, Operations | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.com | M: (415) 555-0192

Evelyn — thanks for the clear synthesis. Quick notes: 

- QBR one-pager looks good at a glance; I can take the slide-outs if we lock the 2 metrics: p50 latency and cost/unit delta vs. baseline. Will update draft and send back by Nov 27 11:30.

- On quantization: can you add a short summary in the tracker of the prompt class where drift is occurring? That will help product decide whether rollback can be partial by customer segment.

- Also flag: finance asked if expediting procurement would change committed TCO for Acme Data (they're in renewal discussion). Markus — can you confirm whether fast-track impacts the customer cost model?

Evelyn / team —

Short answer on procurement: the CloudVendor quote I attached (procurement-timeline-quote.pdf) shows a 3-week lead if we accept the standard configuration. We can shorten to 7–10 business days if we accept an expedited provisioning fee (estimate attached). That expedited path would require the $150k buffer Evelyn mentioned — otherwise we take the longer route and enable burst fallback on hosting. 

Finance note: expediting will not change the committed TCO for contracted customers in year one if Redwood covers the one-time provisioning fee. I flagged this with finance; they requested a formal spend approval if we go that route.

Markus
Director, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Ops OKR synthesis & decision lanes — week of Nov 30

Thanks — made the call after reviewing the drift examples Laura requested. Decision:

- Quantization: approve a graduated rollback approach. Rollback full production to previous model for accounts in active renewals and beta customers showing drift (Acme Data included). Simultaneously, re-run the narrower rollout with a tighter prompt-class gating and additional evals.

Action items assigned:
- Marissa: notify Acme Data and schedule a short remediation window (2 hours maintenance) with them; provide rollback ETA.
- Engineering: run targeted evals for the flagged prompt class (ENG-3) and provide a remediation report by Dec 3.

Markus — you have the procurement ask; approve buffer spend if CloudVendor cannot meet the expedited window. I support using the $150k buffer to avoid SLA slippage.

Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Product Officer | Redwood Inference
